adjudication.evidence: Both P1 and P2 span the same interval (~532–587) with nearly identical onset offsets; residual plots after subtracting either offset show flat, noise-level residuals across N/E during the interval, confirming a sustained platform. The U component shows physical motion (non-flat residuals) but no return to pre-onset level—however, the N/E axes satisfy the definition of a temporary offset: sustained shift followed by opposing return on the same axes. Since P1 and P2 overlap completely and represent the same event, only one genuine platform exists; the numerical tool selects 534–586 as best-supported boundaries, consistent with observed step onset at ~534 and return at ~586 in N/E. No independent permanent step is embedded within.
